rationale: Start with a broad mid-temperature scouting gradient that should elute all 10 compounds within the run while revealing the overall elution window and any critical pairs. The wide composition range and moderate slope give a good first map without being so steep that everything compresses at the front.

All compounds eluted early and with baseline resolution, so the first run used a much wider organic window than needed. Narrowing the gradient to the observed elution window while keeping the same tG and T should improve time efficiency and may spread the clustered mid-run peaks by using the gradient where the analytes actually elute.

The broad window at 20 min already gave full resolution, so now test a much steeper gradient to see how much runtime can be cut before the clustered mid-eluting peaks become limiting. This slope comparison against injection 1 will show whether the critical pairs are strongly slope-sensitive or mostly need temperature/selectivity changes.

The 10 min gradient is very fast but over-compresses the central cluster, while 20 min fully resolves it, so 14 min is a direct interpolation to find the shortest gradient that restores acceptable resolution of pairs 5–7. Keeping the same phi window and temperature isolates slope as the only variable.

The limiting pair 6/7 improves strongly with shallower slope: R goes from 0.46 at 10 min to 1.20 at 14 min and 2.36 at 20 min, so 16 min is the next logical point to target full resolution while staying faster than 20 min. This should be close to the optimum tradeoff between separation and runtime.

Since slope optimization is already near the best tradeoff, probe temperature to see whether the critical 6/7 pair can gain selectivity without lengthening the run. A 5 °C decrease is a small, informative step that may resolve the pair better while keeping the same fast 14 min gradient.

Lowering temperature worsened selectivity by collapsing a different pair, so test the opposite direction at the same gradient to see whether modestly higher temperature improves the critical central cluster. This isolates whether temperature can beat the 14 min, 40 C method without sacrificing speed.

Since 15 min is off-grid and 16 min already gives full resolution with only a tiny time penalty, 18 min tests whether CRF drops monotonically beyond that or whether there is any flat optimum around the resolution-complete region. This also better defines the slope-response curve of the critical cluster for later exploitation.

The broad 0.05–0.95 window is likely wider than needed, and narrowing phi1 while keeping the successful 14 min slope region may improve effective use of the gradient over the central cluster without pushing runtime too high. This tests whether trimming the late, unused high-organic end can boost the limiting 6/7 separation at the current best runtime.

The improvement from lowering phi1 from 0.95 to 0.85 suggests the late high-organic region was wasted; trimming a bit further may keep all peaks inside the useful gradient while improving time enough to raise CRF further. This is a local refinement around the current best method, with the same temperature and tG.

The current best sits between 0.95 and 0.80, with 0.85 outperforming both, so test the other adjacent phi1 setting to bracket the local optimum. This will show whether 0.85 is truly best or whether a slightly wider window recovers a bit more speed or selectivity.

The optimum appears near phi1 0.90 with tG 14, so now test whether raising phi0 trims unused low-organic time and improves the early part of the run without hurting the critical middle cluster. The first peak is still well retained, so a small increase in phi0 is a reasonable local refinement around the current best.

Raising phi0 improved CRF over the 0.05/0.90 method, so test whether restoring a slightly wider upper bound keeps that gain while shortening the last peak further. This is a tight local probe around the current best to see whether the optimum is really at phi1 0.90 or a bit higher when phi0 is 0.10.

With phi0 fixed at 0.10, the optimum phi1 likely lies near 0.90, so the next local bracket is 0.85. This will determine whether the best CRF at 0.10/0.90 is a true maximum or whether a slightly narrower upper bound improves the balance of speed and central-pair resolution.

You have already reached the maximum CRF of 1.000, so the priority is to avoid repeating that exact method while exploring a nearby condition that could be equally good and confirm robustness. Raising phi0 one step tests whether some low-organic range is still unnecessary, but keeps the successful upper bound, slope, and temperature.

You already have multiple methods at the CRF ceiling, so continue mapping the upper edge of phi0 to find the most aggressive starting composition that still preserves full performance. The first peak remains retained at phi0 0.15, so increasing to 0.20 is the next informative robustness test around the proven optimum region.

The best region is now clearly around phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.85, so test whether trimming phi1 one step at the successful phi0 0.15 setting maintains the CRF ceiling with a slightly tighter gradient window. This is a focused robustness check in the local optimum neighborhood.

You have ceiling performance at phi1 0.85, and both lower and higher phi1 values have not yet been checked at phi0 0.15. Testing 0.90 completes the local bracket around the current optimum and may reveal another equally robust max-performing method.

With several 14 min methods already at the CRF ceiling, the only remaining upside is to see whether a slightly steeper gradient can keep full resolution while shortening the run. Using the proven best phi window and dropping tG to 12 min is the most direct test of that possibility.

The 12 min run at phi0 0.10 was close but slightly underresolved at the critical pair, so try the same shorter gradient with the equally optimal phi0 0.15 setting, which previously gave a very similar but slightly faster fully resolved profile at 14 min. This is the best remaining shot at finding a shorter method that still reaches the CRF ceiling.

The maximum CRF is already achieved, so use remaining injections to probe robustness; a larger temperature shift can reveal whether the optimum is stable or highly temperature-sensitive beyond the 35/45 C checks. Testing the best composition program at 25 C gives the most informative endpoint on the low-temperature side.

The 25 C run showed drastic temperature-driven selectivity changes, so the corresponding high-temperature endpoint is the most informative remaining experiment. Running the best composition program at 60 C will define the full thermal robustness window and show whether the severe low-temperature coelutions reverse or simply shift elsewhere.

At 25 C the selectivity collapses badly, so use one of the remaining runs to distinguish whether that failure is mainly thermal or can be mitigated by a shallower gradient. Extending tG to 16 min at the same phi window should reveal whether the low-temperature coelutions are slope-responsive or fundamentally require returning to 40 C.

The 25 C comparison showed the poor selectivity is not rescued by a shallower gradient, so use the penultimate run to make the analogous slope test at 60 C. This will show whether the high-temperature failure is similarly dominated by selectivity rather than gradient steepness, completing the thermal map around the best method.

For the final run, test whether the phi0 0.15 optimum neighborhood also benefits from a slightly shallower gradient, since 16 min at phi0 0.10 was fully resolved but incurred a small time penalty. This completes the local map around the max-performing conditions and checks for another robust ceiling method.
